beats.text: The first bicycle had no pedals at all.
In 1817, Karl Drais built a wooden running machine. You pushed it along with your feet.
In the 1860s, pedals were added to the front wheel. People called it the boneshaker.
To go faster, the front wheel grew huge. The penny-farthing was quick, but falls were brutal.
In 1885, the safety bicycle added a chain to the back wheel, and two equal wheels.
Air-filled tires soon smoothed out the ride.
Today, bikes have light carbon frames, dozens of gears, and even electric motors.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
